key_insight: Modeling how visual states evolve across clips (state transitions and identity consistency) produces more coherent, story-preserving video retrieval than treating clips independently.
problem_solved: Current retrieval methods match clips by local semantics and ignore whether retrieved clips keep a consistent object/actor state and identity across a sequence; this paper formalizes Consistent Video Retrieval (CVR) to address that gap.
method: Define the CVR task and construct a diagnostic benchmark by re-purposing clips from YouCook2, COIN, and CrossTask to evaluate state and identity consistency.

Introduce CAST, a model that explicitly represents visual state embeddings and learns transition dynamics between consecutive clips so retrieval considers how states evolve, not just per-clip similarity.
Train with objectives that combine local semantic alignment with transition- and identity-consistency losses and perform sequence-aware retrieval scoring to prioritize coherent clip sequences.
impact: Enables retrieval systems that assemble clip sequences preserving narrative continuity and actor/object consistency—useful for long-form video editing, story-driven retrieval, and any downstream task requiring coherent multi-clip outputs.

paper_title: CAST: Modeling Visual State Transitions for Consistent Video Retrieval
